name: DSHP-Plus LTSS Self-Directed Attendant Care
summary: Delaware's Diamond State Health Plan-Plus (DSHP-Plus) is the Medicaid managed care program for long-term services at home. Members who need nursing-facility-level care can choose self-directed attendant care and hire their own caregiver, including a friend, neighbor or family member. A financial management services agency pays the caregiver and handles taxes and background checks.
who_qualifies: Delaware resident age 65 or older, or an adult with a physical disability (or certain other qualifying conditions such as HIV/AIDS).
Needs nursing-facility level of care (or is at risk of it), as found by a DMMA Pre-Admission Screening nurse.
Meets Medicaid long-term care financial rules: reported as $2,485/month income and $2,000 in assets for a single person in 2026.
Lives in the community — self-directed attendant care is not offered to people in assisted living or nursing facilities.

who_can_be_paid.adult_children_relatives: yes — managed care policy says members may hire people they have a close personal relationship with, such as a neighbor, friend or family member.
who_can_be_paid.spouse: limited — some guides say spouses can be hired, but Delaware First Health's LTSS policy says people who are legally responsible for the member (which includes a spouse) may not be the attendant; confirm with your MCO.
who_can_be_paid.parent_of_minor: n/a — this adult LTSS option is for adults; children use the separate pediatric self-directed attendant care option.
who_can_be_paid.live_together: optional — the caregiver may live with the member; live-in caregivers are not paid overtime.

pay.detail: Delaware does not publish a self-directed attendant wage. Third-party reports put it around $13–$21/hour (about $16.75 average in 2026). Overtime at 1.5x is paid for hours over 40 a week, except for caregivers who live in the same home as the member.

hours_or_budget: The MCO case manager assesses needs and authorizes attendant hours in the plan of care; the member must show medical necessity. Respite is limited to 14 days a year unless the MCO approves more.

waitlist.detail: DSHP-Plus long-term care is part of Delaware's Medicaid managed care demonstration; people who meet financial and medical rules are enrolled. Eligibility decisions can take up to 3 months.

self_directed_or_agency: Either. Members can use MCO network agencies or self-direct. In self-direction the member (or an employer representative) is the employer and an IRS-approved fiscal/employer agent (FMS) such as Easter Seals, JEVS or GT Independence runs payroll. The employer representative cannot also be the paid attendant.
how_to_apply: Call the DMMA Central Intake Unit at 1-866-940-8963 to request a long-term care application packet.
Schedule the financial eligibility interview and gather proof of income, bank statements and other documents.
Complete the Pre-Admission Screening, where a DMMA nurse decides whether nursing-facility level of care is needed.
After enrollment, tell your MCO case manager you want self-directed attendant care; the FMS agency will help you hire and screen your caregiver.

faqs.q: Can I get paid to care for my parent in Delaware?
faqs.a: Yes. If your parent is on DSHP-Plus long-term care and chooses self-directed attendant care, they can hire you. The FMS agency runs the background checks and pays you.

faqs.q: Can a spouse be paid under DSHP-Plus?
faqs.a: It is unclear. Consumer guides say yes, but at least one Delaware MCO policy bars people legally responsible for the member from being the attendant. Ask your MCO case manager in writing.

faqs.q: How much do self-directed attendants earn?
faqs.a: Delaware does not publish a rate. Reports put pay around $13 to $21 an hour. Overtime is paid above 40 hours a week unless the caregiver lives with the member.

faqs.q: Who can't be the paid attendant?
faqs.a: Anyone serving as the member's employer representative, anyone on the Adult Abuse Registry, a sex offender registry or the excluded-provider list, and people legally responsible for the member.
No waiting list is published. Eligibility can take up to 3 months while DMMA checks finances and level of care.

name: Self-Directed Attendant Care for Children (Non-LTSS Pediatric)
summary: Delaware Medicaid lets families self-direct attendant care for children under 21 who need help with daily activities because of a chronic medical condition, developmental disability or behavioral health condition. A parent or other legally responsible family member can be hired and paid for up to 40 hours a week. Another adult must act as the employer representative.
who_qualifies: Child or young adult under age 21 enrolled in Delaware Medicaid managed care (DSHP).
Has a chronic medical condition, intellectual/developmental disability, or behavioral health condition that causes a need for help with age-appropriate daily activities.
Attendant care is authorized by the MCO (prior authorization is required).
Has a family member or other designee who can act as employer representative.

who_can_be_paid.adult_children_relatives: yes — relatives, friends and neighbors age 18+ who pass background checks can be hired.
who_can_be_paid.parent_of_minor: yes — legally responsible family members, including parents, can be paid for up to 40 hours a week; hours above 40 must go to someone else.
who_can_be_paid.live_together: optional — the paid parent usually lives with the child, but it is not required.

pay.detail: Delaware and its MCOs do not publish a pediatric self-directed attendant wage; the rate is set through the MCO and FMS agency. Ask your MCO for the current rate.

hours_or_budget: The MCO care coordinator assesses the child and authorizes attendant hours. A legally responsible family member may be paid for no more than 40 of those hours each week.

waitlist.detail: No waiting list is published; services depend on Medicaid enrollment and MCO authorization.

self_directed_or_agency: Self-directed. The parent or designee directs care; an FMS agency handles payroll. The person who signs as employer representative cannot be the paid attendant, so two adults are needed if a parent will be paid.
how_to_apply: Ask your child's Delaware Medicaid MCO care coordinator about self-directed attendant care.
Complete the assessment and get prior authorization for attendant hours.
Name an employer representative (not the paid caregiver) and enroll with the FMS agency.
The caregiver completes background checks and an employment agreement before services start.

faqs.q: Can a parent get paid to care for a disabled child in Delaware?
faqs.a: Yes. Under self-directed attendant care for children, a parent or other legally responsible family member can be paid for up to 40 hours a week.

faqs.q: Why do we need a second adult?
faqs.a: The employer representative cannot be the paid attendant. If one parent is paid, the other parent or another adult must sign as employer.

faqs.q: How old can the child be?
What can the attendant help with?
faqs.a: Bathing, dressing, hygiene, transferring, toileting, skin care, eating and mobility, plus some daily-living tasks in the care plan.

faqs.q: When did Delaware start paying parents?
faqs.a: Delaware asked CMS in 2022 to add this option to its 1115 demonstration starting January 1, 2023. MCO policies now list the 40-hour limit for legally responsible family members.
